Yes. The moment you get the visa, you should be able to travel freely. Make sure to ask for the multiple reentry sticker. You should get two stickers in your passport. One is the visa, the other allows you to travel freely in and out of Israel (provided you keep it within reasonable limits of 3 months max per year).
Regarding your dad, I do not know. It is recommended to apply for a family visitor visa to minimize the risk that there will be an issue at the border. Not sure if the ETA asks for the criminal history. If yes, I would probably consult a local lawyer. Obviously if they ask about prior arrests or a criminal record, the Israeli assessment will greatly differ based on the nature of the crime. Not asking what it was, that's none of my business, but obviously tax evasion would not be a big deal while drug or violent crime might be.
I don't actually remember that they asked about criminal history on the ETA I filled out some time ago for a family member. 

More info on ETA requirements are here:
https://aic.org.il/eta-il-how-to-apply-and-everything-you-need-to-know-guide/
